Tulare County CA Tax Sale – Buy Property for Less Than a Down Payment

What if you could buy land or a house for less than what most people pay just for a down payment?

Tulare County is auctioning off tax-defaulted properties, and the starting bids are often just the amount of unpaid taxes. That means investors can walk away with property for a fraction of the market price.

Quick Overview: Tax Sale Details

Why Tulare County is a Great Place for Property Investors

  • Properties often start at very low prices, based on unpaid taxes only
  • The auction is completely online, so you can participate from anywhere
  • High activity in Visalia and Porterville makes the area attractive for flips and rentals
  • Large parcels of farmland are common, making it ideal for agricultural investment
  • Since it’s a tax deed sale, there’s no redemption period—the property is yours after you pay

What You Need to Know Before You Bid

  • Always research the property beforehand. Some may have liens, be landlocked, or come with legal issues
  • These properties are sold “as-is” with no inspections, no guarantees
  • If you want full legal ownership or to resell later, you might need a quiet title action

Interesting Facts About Tulare County Real Estate

  • Tulare County is one of the top agricultural producers in the U.S., known for dairy, citrus, and nut crops
  • Housing here is more affordable than in California’s coastal regions
  • Cities like Visalia and Porterville are growing quickly, making them attractive for long-term investors
  • Many auction properties are vacant land or farmland, offering unique investment opportunities

Local Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Outdoor activities include access to nearby national parks like Sequoia and Kings Canyon
  • Transportation is easy with Highway 99 running through the county and regional airports nearby
  • Key industries include agriculture, logistics, healthcare, and education
  • Tulare County is known for its small-town feel with growing amenities and infrastructure

Frequently Asked Questions

Can anyone bid in the auction?
Yes. Anyone, including out-of-state and international investors, can bid if they register and pay the deposit.

Do I own the property right away?
Yes. Since it’s a tax deed sale, there is no redemption period. Once you pay, the county records the deed in your name.

What happens if the property has liens or unpaid utility bills?
Some liens may stay with the property. It’s important to check the title and property records before bidding.

Can I inspect the property before the auction?
No. These properties are sold “as-is,” and there’s no guarantee you’ll be able to access them beforehand.

How do I pay if I win?
You must pay by wire transfer or cashier’s check. Personal checks and credit cards are not accepted.

Pro Tips for First-Time Bidders

  • Start with one or two properties to get used to the process
  • Review the property records from the Assessor’s and Recorder’s offices
  • Stick to a budget during the auction—avoid overbidding
  • Learn about quiet title actions if you plan to resell or refinance the property
